quests.question: The box of chocolates ___ on the top shelf.
quests.hint: Find the single main noun before 'of' and ignore what comes after it.
quests.explanation: The subject is 'the box', a singular noun; 'of chocolates' just describes what's inside it. Singular subjects take the -s form: 'sits'.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement follows the head noun before a prepositional phrase, not the noun inside it

quests.question: The captain of the players ___ the pre-game meeting.
quests.hint: 'Of the players' describes the captain - it doesn't make the subject plural.
quests.explanation: 'The captain' is the true subject, and it's singular, even though 'the players' (plural) appears right after it. The verb takes -s: 'leads'.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement follows the head noun before a prepositional phrase, not the noun inside it

quests.question: The list of ingredients ___ printed on the back of the package.
quests.hint: Locate the noun that the whole sentence is actually about.
quests.explanation: 'The list' is singular, and 'of ingredients' only tells us what kind of list it is. The verb agrees with 'list': 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement follows the head noun before a prepositional phrase, not the noun inside it

quests.question: The keys to the house ___ missing.
quests.hint: This time the main noun is plural - don't let the singular noun after it change your answer.
quests.explanation: 'The keys' is the plural subject; 'to the house' is singular but doesn't affect agreement. Plural subjects take the base form: 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement follows the head noun before a prepositional phrase, even when it's plural and the phrase after it is singular

quests.question: The winners of the contest ___ their prize next week.
quests.hint: Check the noun right at the start of the subject, not the noun tucked inside the phrase.
quests.explanation: 'The winners' is plural, and 'of the contest' is just extra detail. Plural subjects use the base verb form: 'receive'.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement follows the head noun before a prepositional phrase, even when it's plural and the phrase after it is singular

quests.question: The pages of the report ___ numbered incorrectly.
quests.hint: 'Report' is singular, but is it actually the subject of this sentence?
quests.explanation: 'The pages' is the true subject and is plural; 'of the report' just specifies which pages. The verb takes the base form: 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement follows the head noun before a prepositional phrase, even when it's plural and the phrase after it is singular

quests.question: The results, surprisingly, ___ consistent across all three tests.
quests.hint: The word set off by commas is just an aside - it doesn't belong to the subject.
quests.explanation: 'The results' is the plural subject; 'surprisingly' is just a comment inserted between commas. Plural subjects take the base form: 'remain'.
quests.grammarRule: Parenthetical adverb between subject and verb does not affect agreement

quests.question: The new manager, unfortunately, ___ little experience in this field.
quests.hint: Skip over the word between the commas and connect the subject directly to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'The new manager' is singular; 'unfortunately' is a parenthetical comment that doesn't change the subject. Singular subjects take 'has'.
quests.grammarRule: Parenthetical adverb between subject and verb does not affect agreement

quests.question: This recipe, surprisingly, ___ very few ingredients.
quests.hint: Treat the commas like parentheses - what's inside them can be ignored for agreement.
quests.explanation: 'This recipe' is singular; the word between the commas doesn't change that. The verb takes -s: 'requires'.
quests.grammarRule: Parenthetical adverb between subject and verb does not affect agreement

quests.question: The recipe, one of my grandmother's favorites, ___ only five ingredients.
quests.hint: The phrase between the commas adds a compliment about the subject, not a new subject.
quests.explanation: 'The recipe' remains singular even though the parenthetical phrase mentions 'my grandmother's favorites'. The verb takes -s: 'needs'.
quests.grammarRule: Parenthetical noun phrase does not change the number of the subject

quests.question: The bridge, an engineering marvel from the 1930s, ___ thousands of cars every day.
quests.hint: The phrase between the commas restates or praises the subject - it isn't a second subject.
quests.explanation: 'The bridge' is singular; the descriptive phrase between the commas doesn't add a new subject. The verb takes -s: 'carries'.
quests.grammarRule: Parenthetical noun phrase does not change the number of the subject

quests.question: The twins, both excellent students, ___ the same university next fall.
quests.hint: The description between the commas confirms something about the subject - it doesn't change its number.
quests.explanation: 'The twins' is plural, and 'both excellent students' just adds detail. Plural subjects take the base form: 'attend'.
quests.grammarRule: Parenthetical noun phrase does not change the number of the subject

quests.question: The photos taken during the trip ___ stored on my laptop.
quests.hint: The phrase describing when the photos were taken doesn't change how many photos there are.
quests.explanation: 'The photos' is the plural subject; 'taken during the trip' just describes them. Plural subjects take the base form: 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: Participial (descriptive) phrase attached to the subject does not affect agreement

quests.question: The employee hired last month ___ already impressed the whole team.
quests.hint: 'Hired last month' tells you when, not how many - keep your focus on the subject itself.
quests.explanation: 'The employee' is singular; 'hired last month' is a descriptive phrase, not a second subject. Singular subjects take 'has'.
quests.grammarRule: Participial (descriptive) phrase attached to the subject does not affect agreement

quests.question: The documents needed for the visa application ___ notarized copies.
quests.hint: The phrase explaining why the documents are needed doesn't affect their number.
quests.explanation: 'The documents' is plural; 'needed for the visa application' just adds a reason. Plural subjects take the base form: 'require'.
quests.grammarRule: Participial (descriptive) phrase attached to the subject does not affect agreement

quests.instruction: MATCH THE SUBJECT TO THE VERB
quests.question: The color of her eyes ___ everyone at first glance.
quests.hint: 'Of her eyes' describes the color - it isn't the subject itself.
quests.explanation: 'The color' is singular, and 'of her eyes' simply specifies whose color it is. Singular subjects take -s: 'strikes'.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement follows the head noun before an 'of' phrase, not the noun within it

quests.instruction: MATCH THE SUBJECT TO THE VERB
quests.question: The cost of the repairs ___ higher than we expected.
quests.hint: Compare 'the cost' and 'the repairs' - which one is really doing the being?
quests.explanation: 'The cost' is singular; 'of the repairs' just tells us what the cost refers to. The verb agrees with 'cost': 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement follows the head noun before an 'of' phrase, not the noun within it

quests.instruction: MATCH THE SUBJECT TO THE VERB
quests.question: The names of the winners ___ posted on the board.
quests.hint: 'Names' is plural here, even though 'of the winners' also sounds plural - check the actual head noun.
quests.explanation: 'The names' is the plural subject; 'of the winners' just clarifies whose names they are. Plural subjects take the base form: 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement follows the head noun before an 'of' phrase, not the noun within it

quests.question: My friend, a talented musician, ___ in three bands.
quests.hint: The phrase between the commas renames 'my friend' - it doesn't add a second subject.
quests.explanation: 'My friend' is singular, and 'a talented musician' just identifies who that friend is. Singular subjects take -s: 'plays'.
quests.grammarRule: Appositive phrase does not change the number of the subject it renames

quests.question: The Andersons, our next-door neighbors, ___ moving to Denver next month.
quests.hint: The phrase between the commas just identifies who the Andersons are.
quests.explanation: 'The Andersons' is plural, and 'our next-door neighbors' restates who they are without changing that. Plural subjects take 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: Appositive phrase does not change the number of the subject it renames

quests.question: Mount Kilimanjaro, the tallest peak in Africa, ___ climbers from around the world every year.
quests.hint: The phrase between the commas is just an identifying label for the mountain.
quests.explanation: 'Mount Kilimanjaro' is a singular subject; the appositive just adds a fact about it. The verb takes -s: 'attracts'.
quests.grammarRule: Appositive phrase does not change the number of the subject it renames

quests.question: The instructions on the back of the box ___ hard to follow.
quests.hint: Even with two phrases stacked together, only the very first noun counts as the subject.
quests.explanation: 'The instructions' is the plural subject; 'on the back of the box' is a chain of descriptive detail. Plural subjects take 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: Stacked prepositional phrases do not change the true subject of the sentence

quests.question: The manager of the store on Fifth Avenue ___ every new hire personally.
quests.hint: Ignore both phrases after 'manager' and focus on that one noun.
quests.explanation: 'The manager' is singular, no matter how many phrases follow it. The verb takes -s: 'trains'.
quests.grammarRule: Stacked prepositional phrases do not change the true subject of the sentence

quests.question: The condition of the roads after the storm ___ dangerous.
quests.hint: Trace back through both phrases to the one noun that the sentence is really about.
quests.explanation: 'The condition' is singular; both 'of the roads' and 'after the storm' are extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'remains'.
quests.grammarRule: Stacked prepositional phrases do not change the true subject of the sentence

quests.question: The tone of her messages ___ often misunderstood by coworkers.
quests.hint: The noun right before the blank isn't always the real subject - trace back to the very start.
quests.explanation: 'The tone' is the true subject and is singular, even though 'her messages' (plural) sits right before the verb. The verb agrees with 'tone': 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement follows the true head noun, even when a different-number noun sits right before the verb

quests.question: The reasons behind his decision ___ unclear to the team.
quests.hint: Don't let the singular noun right before the verb fool you - check the very first noun instead.
quests.explanation: 'The reasons' is the true subject and is plural, even though 'his decision' (singular) appears just before the verb. The verb takes the base form: 'remain'.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement follows the true head noun, even when a different-number noun sits right before the verb

quests.question: The safety of the passengers ___ always the airline's top priority.
quests.hint: The plural noun closest to the verb can be misleading - find the actual subject first.
quests.explanation: 'The safety' is singular and is the true subject, even though 'the passengers' (plural) comes right before the verb. The verb agrees with 'safety': 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: Agreement follows the true head noun, even when a different-number noun sits right before the verb

quests.question: The manager of the regional offices, always calm under pressure, ___ every crisis efficiently.
quests.hint: Combine what you've learned: trace past the 'of' phrase and the parenthetical description to the true subject.
quests.explanation: 'The manager' is singular; both 'of the regional offices' and the parenthetical description are extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'handles'.
quests.grammarRule: Identifying the head noun through an 'of' phrase and a parenthetical description

quests.question: The results of the survey, published last week, ___ a shift in public opinion.
quests.hint: Two interruptions in a row - an 'of' phrase and a descriptive phrase - still don't change the subject.
quests.explanation: 'The results' is plural; 'of the survey' and 'published last week' are both extra detail. Plural subjects take the base form: 'show'.
quests.grammarRule: Identifying the head noun through an 'of' phrase and a participial phrase

quests.question: The photographs in this exhibit, taken over three decades, ___ the city's transformation.
quests.hint: As a final check, trace past the prepositional phrase and the descriptive phrase to the real subject.
quests.explanation: 'The photographs' is plural; 'in this exhibit' and 'taken over three decades' both describe it without changing its number. The verb takes the base form: 'capture'.
quests.grammarRule: Identifying the head noun through a prepositional phrase and a participial phrase
